evidence.quote: Constrain references to existing rows; null references are allowed unless separately forbidden. Before starting a transaction, enable enforcement on each connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON, then query PRAGMA foreign_keys and check that it returns 1.

evidence.quote: Often a better fit when many machines need shared database access or competing writes cannot take turns. SQLite can still be suitable behind an application server with local storage.

evidence.quote: WAL still allows only one writer, and its shared-memory design requires processes on the same machine.

sourceChecks.claim: Appropriate-uses page supports application-local storage, direct embedded use and contrast with server databases; engine/file diagram is accurate.
Page explicitly supports embedded/mobile/local applications and suitable websites, with concurrency/locality caveats rather than a toy-only rule.

STRICT page confirms affinity conversion and ANY exception. https://www.sqlite.org/foreignkeys.html confirms enabling and querying enforcement per connection outside a transaction; constraint links support explicit null rules.

Synchronous pragma documents journal/mode-dependent crash durability, including WAL NORMAL recent-commit loss; isolation source supplies hidden incomplete changes. Transaction boundary excludes external HTTP work.
Isolation documentation confirms serialized writers across connections and busy-snapshot failure needing transaction restart. Bounded waits reduce brief contention without guaranteeing success.

WAL documentation verifies append/snapshot overlap, one writer, shared-memory same-host restriction, checkpoint stopping for old readers and possible growth. Diagram shows committed WAL state awaiting checkpoint, not automatic main-file completeness.
Queryplanner explains composite searching/sorting and planner choice; https://www.sqlite.org/eqp.html confirms plan inspection. Index/local CPU-I/O/storage costs remain bounded qualitative claims.

Backup API yields a consistent source snapshot; WAL documentation identifies WAL as persistent state that must accompany the database if outstanding. https://www.sqlite.org/lang_altertable.html describes rebuild/copy migrations; restore tests are appropriate validation rather than an asserted recovery result.

Appropriate-uses checklist supports client/server for network-separated shared access or write demand unable to take turns, while allowing local SQLite behind an application service. No numeric workload cutoff asserted.
